phases.title: Getting started
phases.goalLine: Learn the controls on a small practice scene.

steps.body:
Welcome! Please use a mouse on a desktop or laptop for this study.

You are looking at several 3D surface scans of the same place, taken at different times. Over the next few minutes you will learn to move around, inspect differences between the scans, and align them. Press Continue when you are ready.
Drag with the left mouse button to orbit around the scene, and use the mouse wheel over empty background (or hold Alt) to zoom. Try both now.
Several scans overlap here. Move the mouse over the surface and scroll the wheel to cycle which scan layer is picked. The name of the active layer appears under the cursor.
Pins mark a spot you want to study. Press the ○ Pin button in the bar, click a point on the surface, then press ✓ Commit in the panel that appears.
Each committed pin has a card with measurements. Click the pin's marker in the 3D view to open its card.
Look at the distance data in the pin card. Each scan gets one entry, measured relative to the reference scan.

options: It is zero by definition — all distances are measured relative to it
It shows the absolute elevation of the terrain
It shows the number of points in the scan

steps.body: Now align the scans. Open the registration card (⚙ button on the right). 1) Pick a reference scan (★). 2) Place and commit two more pins on solid ground, and enable 'Use as registration landmark' on each pin's card — accept the suggested anchor points. 3) Press 'Solve coarse', look at the preview, and press ✓ Commit.
One quick check about what you just did.

options: It applies the previewed alignment and records a step in the history
It deletes all pins from the scene
It changes which scan is the reference

steps.body: And one about choosing good landmark pins.

options: Pins on stable ground that looks the same in every scan
Pins on surfaces that move or change between scans
Pins placed in empty space next to the terrain

phases.title: Inspect the glacier
phases.goalLine: Get an overview: which parts move, which parts are stable bedrock?

steps.body:
This is the real scene: satellite elevation scans of a glacier, taken in different years. The glacier tongue flows and thins over time, while the surrounding bedrock stays put.

Use the layer panel (☰ Layers) to see the epochs, and Ctrl-click anywhere to get a quick distance probe.
Using the layer panel, count the scan epochs in this dataset.
Where is the moving ice? Mark one point that you believe lies on the glacier tongue.

phases.title: Register the epochs
phases.goalLine: Place ≥3 pins on bedrock, solve coarse then fine, commit both.

steps.body:
Before measuring change, the epochs must be aligned on terrain that did NOT change — the bedrock. Alignment computed on moving ice would absorb the very signal you want to measure.

Your goal: at least 3 landmark pins on bedrock, a committed coarse solve, then a committed fine (ICP) solve.
Work through the registration: commit at least 3 pins on bedrock and enable each as a landmark, pick a reference epoch (★), Solve coarse → Commit, then Solve fine → Commit.

phases.title: Evaluate the result
phases.goalLine: How good is your registration, and how do you know?

steps.body: Compare the epochs over bedrock after your registration. Which statement fits your result best?

options: All epochs agree closely over bedrock
Most epochs agree, one or two are clearly off

steps.body: After a successful bedrock-based registration, the remaining offsets over STABLE terrain should be…

options: Equal to the glacier's annual motion

steps.body: If the stable-terrain RMS drops from 4.3 m to 0.8 m when you commit a solve, the registration has…

phases.title: A second opinion
phases.goalLine: Try the all-terrain ICP a colleague suggested, then keep the better result.

steps.body:
A colleague suggests skipping the landmark pins: 'just run plain ICP on everything, it uses all the data'.

Try it: switch the ICP mode in the registration card, run one more fine solve, and compare. Keep whichever state you trust more — use ↩ rollback if needed — then press '★ Set as final'.
Run one more fine solve with the OTHER ICP mode, decide which result to keep (commit, rollback or discard as needed), then press '★ Set as final' in the registration card.
Which result did you keep, and why?

phases.title: Measure the change
phases.goalLine: How much did the surface change at the two flagged spots?

steps.body: Two flags mark spots of interest. For each: place a pin at the flag, open its card, and read off how far the newest epoch lies above or below the reference (signed, in metres).
Flag 1 (western flag): signed surface change of the newest epoch relative to the reference, in metres.
Flag 2 (eastern flag): signed surface change of the newest epoch relative to the reference, in metres.
In one or two sentences: what happened to this glacier between the epochs?

phases.title: Wrap up
phases.goalLine: A few questions about your experience, then your completion code.

steps.body: How did working with the system feel? (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)
How demanding was the task? (0 = very low, 100 = very high)
About the visualization itself. (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree)
How often do you work with 3D tools (games, CAD, GIS, modelling)?
How familiar are you with geosciences or surveying?

That's it — thank you for taking part!
